# 1. Executive Summary LOCKED The project is a focused, few-hour survival-horror adventure built around exploration, environmental puzzles, scent-driven pursuit, temporary defensive combat, and escape from one interconnected Goth style-themed location.

1.1 Main Pitch In Napoleonic-era France, the player explores a sealed Gothic mansion or castle (TBD based on project scope and available assets) while a persistent werewolf follows their scent. The player must solve area-based puzzles, manage finite silver ammunition and odor-masking supplies, use safe havens to save progress and craft utilities, and ultimately escape a creature that can be delayed but never permanently killed.

1.2 Game Snapshot Category Current Design Genre Stealth, walking adventure, atmospheric survival horror, environmental puzzle adventure. Player fantasy Survive as a vulnerable but resourceful person who learns the building, reads a predator, and turns scarce historical objects into temporary protection. Primary objective Survive - Explore the environment, solve the required puzzle chains, open an escape route, and leave the trapped location. Failure Immediate game over when the werewolf physically reaches the player. Opposing force One persistent werewolf that searches all active zones and cannot be permanently killed. Playtime Approximately 2-4 hours for a first playthrough; final target depends on area count and puzzle density. World scope One mansion or castle, organized into 3-5 major areas plus supporting rooms and optional spaces. Perspective Final choice open until equivalent first-person and third-person prototypes are compared. Platform / engine / rating PC / Unreal / T Rating

1.3 Design Pillars Pillar Player-facing promise Design test Persistent Predator The werewolf is an active presence that searches, tracks and re-enters the player’s plans rather than waiting only in scripted scenes. Outside safe havens, the player regularly makes choices based on where the werewolf may be and how strongly it can track them. Readable Lethality The creature is deadly, but major attacks have recognizable cues and consistent counterplay. Players can identify a pounce preparation and explain why a capture occurred. Scarcity with Agency Silver, gunpowder and odor supplies are finite, so every use is a strategic decision rather than routine combat. The game remains finishable after resources are wasted, but the route becomes substantially harder. v0.2 | CONCEPT / PRE-PRODUCTION | PAGE 2 Pillar Player-facing promise Design test Atmospheric Discovery Rooms, objects, sound and architecture communicate the environment, puzzles and history. Players can orient themselves and infer puzzle logic without constant objective markers. Temporary Relief Safe havens and successful neutralizations create short periods of control without eliminating the long-term threat. Relief is meaningful, limited and followed by renewed uncertainty.

1.4 Scope Boundaries Ships in the focused game Deferred, optional or explicitly excluded One persistent werewolf; one interconnected mansion/castle; 3-5 major areas; area-specific puzzles; scent, sight and hearing; pounce and high-speed charge; hiding; finite silver ammunition; two flintlock weapons; odor masking; 2-3 safe havens; autosave; one complete escape path. Permanent werewolf kill; enemy roster expansion; conventional action-combat progression; random resource respawns; dodge roll; complex parkour; open world; multiplayer; procedural level generation. Optional if production supports it: door breaking, werewolf-only shortcuts, castle walls, underground dungeons, and advanced odor interactions. Any feature that requires substantial new animation, destruction, navigation or content without strengthening the core loop.
